segments.text: So, then, it was reported in the Korean media in the past months that the Navy plans to acquire two more Malvar-class missile frigates.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: In addition, the two frigates ordered last year, so that would be the fifth and sixth guided missile frigate of the Navy.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: Are you at liberty to confirm this proposal?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Definitely, Your Honor. There is an intent, really, to acquire.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: The trigger has not yet been pulled.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: And also, every budget hearing, I make this follow-up regarding the upgrading and the completion,

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: the installation of the still-unfitted sensors and weapon system for the Rizal-class and Malvar-class.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Your Honor, they are ongoing.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: Thank you. Thank you.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: So, also, some people ask me to relate this to you.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: How about the plan?

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: As for the acquisition of multi-role fighters, I know that this is a very complicated matter.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: And for additional air defense missiles.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: And also, coastal defense missiles.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: It's still there, Your Honor, depending on the financing that we need.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: But now, knowing what we know, we have to have a lot of systems in place before any multi-role fighter is acquired.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Because a multi-role fighter...

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: A multi-role fighter, as we saw recently, is heavily dependent on ground control and domain awareness.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: If not, it will be an unguided pilot-controlled aircraft, and its use will be marginal.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: So, maybe it's, Your Honor, without an air-to-air refueling, it will not be able to take off with adequate stores.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: And if we do not have the adequate hangarage facilities to service it, it will be useless, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: So, it comes as a force package.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: And as we learned, the minimum force package is 40 at any one mission, actually, for external defense.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: So, maybe, really, the amendment of PD 415 can help.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: It can help in obtaining funding for your programs.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: So, finally, Madam Chair, the Secretary, of course, is aware that it is the Executive Department

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: that prepared this program of expenditures under the Constitution, not the Congress.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: And Congress has no power to increase the appropriations proposed by the President.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: We can do that, but we will get it from other items, which is very difficult on the part of Congress to do.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: So, the real battle here is at the level of the DBCC, the DBM, not here in Congress.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: I believe the connectivity and infrastructure are also necessary, Your Honor, for us to perform our mission roles.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: So, if the infrastructure budget will support the weight, really, of the equipment we need,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: it will solve a lot of our problems, too, on logistics.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: And I think that's the emphasis.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Of course, on education, too.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: And Madam Chair, no more questions.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: But in spite of budgetary constraints, our AFP and DND, they are doing their best to secure our territory and our sovereignty.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: So, on behalf of the people of my district, let me extend my sincerest appreciation to them.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arnan C. Panaligan
segments.text: Thank you for your service to our officers and men.

segments.speaker: Rep. Bella Vanessa B. Suansing
segments.text: Thank you, Congressman Panaligan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Bella Vanessa B. Suansing
segments.text: Next to interpolate, Congressman Arlyn Ayon from the minority.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: Thank you, Madam Chair.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Secretary, to our distinguished members of the committee, our officers and men of the Armed Forces of the Philippines,

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: and all the officials and guests present here today.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: First, I would like to express my appreciation to you, Mr. Secretary, for your leadership and for the various initiatives you have undertaken

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: to strengthen our national defense.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Secretary.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: I am one of those who strongly support the Department of National Defense.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: Coming from Bukidnon, a province that has experienced the reality of insurgency,

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: I have personally witnessed how our gallant men and women of the Armed Forces of the Philippines

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: have courageously protected our communities and our nation.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: Today, we are very happy to share that Bukidnon has become one of our country's emerging tourist destination.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: And I believe that this progress has been made possible in large part because of the stable peace and security that our province now enjoys.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: Our active soldiers have contributed tremendously, not only for our national security, but also to our economic and national development.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: But, Mr. Secretary, I would also like to take this opportunity to highlight our veterans, both our uniformed personnel and the civilian human resources

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: who have devoted many years to the defense of our country.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: I believe that we must never forget that these heroes who once carried the burden of protecting our nation.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: May I therefore ask, Mr. Secretary, in the Department's plans and budget priorities,

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: have we given equal weight and importance to the welfare of our veterans throughout the country,

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: particularly those who are now elderly and facing increasing health care and living expenses?

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: And finally, how can we as lawmakers work together with the Department to properly honor these heroes,

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: not merely through words of gratitude, but through concrete programs, adequate benefits, health care,

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: and support for those who are suffering from illnesses and long-term effects of the stress, trauma, and sacrifices they endured in the service of our nation?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Thank you very much to the distinguished colleague, former distinguished member of the House.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: I believe that it's well appropriate that you raise the issue.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: And I think what we should do, really, is to decouple.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: We should decouple the veterans' pensions from active duty salaries.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: So we can adjust their pensions without adjusting necessarily the pay increases for our active duty personnel.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Actually, the recent increases in pay were due to a compromise we reached with the

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: veterans to increase their pension rates 5% for three years, in total 15% by 2028.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: But unless the increases are decoupled by law from the active duty rates,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: you need to increase the rates of the active duty personnel.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Secondly, Your Honor, we are trying really to reach out to them.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: And we still are hopefully going to be able to launch our first hospice hopefully by the end of the year

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: for taking care of the older veterans who have no place to call home

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: and who are forced to be confined in hospitals.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Because there's nowhere else to go.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Our issue there is the accreditation of the caregivers and the finding of caregivers

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: and the building of the facility.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Nonetheless, we have to get our feet wet with it in order to provide them adequate

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: a place where they can retire with dignity.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Thirdly, Your Honor, it's knowing fully well that

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: the veterans need to adequate socialization, if not some of them confined to home really suffer.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: And I've seen it with even younger veterans who were very active before but when withdrawn from their comfort zone,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: so to speak, have become.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Have become, you know, very withdrawn and their families talk to me about it.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Fourthly, Your Honor, a lot of the predicament of veterans in terms of health

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: can be addressed preventively while they are still in active duty.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: That's why the active duty care right now, when we are seeing the onset of diseases like heart disease,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: diabetes,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: heart attacks at a younger age, right now at 35,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: we've seen a lot of people really get affected by strokes.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: So we'll have to be more proactive in monitoring the diseases

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: which may exacerbate their situation when they become veterans and require extensive care,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: which could have been prevented.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: So it's not a big deal for us to do that.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: But it is a big problem and it's not something that is perfectly anticipated

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: had we known of the situation beforehand.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: So, Your Honor, I think on the pension system, while not opposed to pension reform,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: I think the key there is not to lump the AFP retirees with the others.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: I know it's kind of controversial, but the AFP is a national force that is part of the national system.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: receives no subsidies from any other agency.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Unlike, let's say, the BFP or the PNP,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: they have more roles with the local communities that they are there to serve.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: And so the basis of the pension on the basis of fairness should be segregated

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: and agencies or communities which derive benefits from directed or targeted services

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: like PJMP or PNP should share in the pension burden.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Unlike the AFP, which is a purely sovereign and national force.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: I realize, really, that there will come a time when pensions, if not reformed now,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: will be more important.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Will eat up.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: will eat up a lot of fiscal space.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Nonetheless, if at this day and age,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: at this stage of our national development

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: where the AFP is fully engaged with the law troop ceiling

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: on several mission areas 365 days of the year,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: I think they need the peace of mind.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: And since the retirees also form part of the AFP family

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: who are there helping each and every step of the way,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: I think at this stage, it's best the pension be studied

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: unlike the old RSPS system which was not a sustainable system.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: And until we are...

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: We are sure that there is a full-proof system

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: which will guarantee them peace of mind when they retire

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: and which will motivate them to commit themselves.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: And if not the same way, perhaps even a greater way

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: to mission accomplishment,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: then I think it's best to err on the side of giving peace of mind

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: to our activities.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: To our duty personnel and our veterans.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Secretary.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: That's our concern.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: So hopefully, and can BND assure this committee

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: that no Filipino veterans who serve our country honorably

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: will be left behind because of lack of funds,

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: delayed benefits, or inadequate health care?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Rest assured, we are at the forefront of fighting for veterans' benefits.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: And my personal connection with our close relationship

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: with veterans' groups of whatever sort,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: and particularly even our retired enlisted personnel

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: and our retired NCOs and civilian personnel

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: because they develop a lot of expertise.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Post-retirement, actually, we still try to use them as best as we can.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Keeping them occupied.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: At the same time, while training the next generation

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: of people who will succeed in leadership positions, particularly.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Secretary.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: That will be all, Madam Chairman.

segments.speaker: Rep. Arlyn P. Ayon
segments.text: Thank you.

segments.speaker: Rep. Bella Vanessa B. Suansing
segments.text: Thank you to the other.

segments.speaker: Rep. Bella Vanessa B. Suansing
segments.text: Thank you, Congressman Ayon.

segments.speaker: Rep. Bella Vanessa B. Suansing
segments.text: Next interpellate, Congressman Munir Erbison from the majority.

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: Magandang umaga, Madam Chairman.

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: Magandang umaga sa lahat.

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: Just want to make a manifestation.

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: I would like to express my full support for the Department of National Defense

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: and recognize its important role in maintaining peace and security

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: in the 2nd District of Sulu.

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: We are grateful to the DND and the Armed Forces of the Philippines

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: for their continued presence and support.

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: In our communities, their efforts have helped us sustain peace

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: and create a better environment for the development of the province of Sulu.

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: We hope for their continued support as we work together to preserve peace

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: and progress we have achieved.

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: Dati-dati, ang tinatanong ng mga kababayan natin,

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: Kumusta ng Sulu?

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: Ang daming sabi niya mga problema.

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: Pero ngayon, ang tinatanong kung anong magandang beach sa Sulu kasi peaceful.

segments.speaker: Rep. Munir N. Arbison Jr.
segments.text: Maraming salamat.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Papasalamat po ako, magsukul, sa ating kapatid na taga-Sulu.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Malaki pong tulong sa atin ang katahimikan sa Sulu.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: At iyan po ay magbibigay po ng oportunidad sa ating WestMinCom.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Lalo na ang Naval Forces West.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Na mag-perform po ng functions to guard the Sulu Sea passage na papasok

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: sa ating major sea lane or international sea lane of communication sa internal waters po natin.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: So marami pong salamat sa dati kong classmate, si Congressman Arbison,

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: sa katahimikan, sa Sulu, at hope to see you soon.

segments.speaker: Rep. Bella Vanessa B. Suansing
segments.text: Thank you. Thank you, Congressman Munir Arbison.

segments.speaker: Rep. Bella Vanessa B. Suansing
segments.text: Next to interpellate from the minority, Congressman Antonio Tinio.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: Salamat, Chair. Meron pong powerpoint kung pwede. Pero tutuloy ko na habang hihintay natin. Una yung tungkol pa rin sa pension reform, MUP pension reform. Nung 2015 ang budget para sa MUP pension was 68.6 billion. Ngayong 2027, the proposed budget for pension is 154 billion. So mahigit nag-doble na po. Nag-discuss na kanina pero sumasang-ayon po ba ang DND na urgent. Kailangan na pong mapatupad yung pag-reforma. At ang pinaka-reforma na kailangan ay kailangan magkaroon na ng contribution system ang AFP at uniformed personnel, katulad nung ibang mga government employees at saka private na nagkocontribute sa SSS, may counterpart, at doon ang gagaling ang pensyon. Hindi yung kasalukuyan na buong-buo na sinasubsidized ng GAA.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Ito po ang aking kasagutan. Yung 154 po, katulad nung naipaliwanag dating kanina, 49% lang po doon ang nasa AFP. Umakyat po dahil humingi po ang ating mga veterano ng adjustment. Dahil wala pong adjustment for the past years. Ako po hindi po tutol sa pension reform, lamang kung papaano ito ma-implement. Kailangan po pag-aaralan natin ang efekto ng engganyo na sumama po sa serbisyo. And actually, yung risk po na hinaharap na pwede pong lalong-lalo na po yung mga totally disabled na bata, yun po ang talagang malaki. Kasi automatic discharge po na magkakaroon siya ng benefits based on his current rank. So hindi po ako tutol kahit nasa contributions but when will we start it and who will be affected. So it has to be studied. And the most important thing po is to separate the armed forces from the rest of the civilian agencies. Katulad po ng PNP at saka BJMP, part of the service is local or a major part. So it's also fair that the LGUs share the pension burden. Ngayon po, yung disposable income po nila naiiwan din sa pamilya. Hindi wala po akong debate yung mga teacher natin. Malaki din po ang risk. Lalo-lalo na nakikita po natin yung teacher na tumatawid sa baha para pumunta lang sa eskwelahan. Ngunit ang pakiusap lang, pag-aaralan po itong mabuti at kung kailan po i-implement.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: So, Chair, pakalawang beses binanggit ni Secretary yung pangangailangan ihiwalay yung pension ng military sa civilian uniform. I suppose. So, yun yung police, BJMP, Bucor, etc. At ang kuha ko sa sinasabi nyo, dapat may contribution din ng LGU sa kanilang pensyon. Could you elaborate on this? Parang ngayon ko lang narinig ang ganitong proposal. Parang sinasabi, ngayon, national government ang buong-buong nagbabayad ng pensyon. So, ang sinasuggest nyo ba dapat kalgahinan ng LGU? At least a part of it? Of the civilian uniform personnel pension?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Opo, dapat pag-aaralan po natin. Hindi ko po sinasabi that is one way. Pero kailangan po i-examine po natin dahil ang servisyo ng police is basically local, no? Except for national crime-fighting authorities. So, in terms of burden sharing, dahil yung era po, alam naman po natin that that goes in block, which is undiminished. I think we might want to study the fiscal impact of burden sharing for them. I'm not saying that that's a cut-and-dried solution. Pero tingnan po natin para naman ma-ease yung pension burden ng ating national government.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: Okay. Ngayon ko lang narinig ito na burden sharing ang ibig sabihin ipakarga yung pensyon ng police. At iba pang uniform aside from military sa LGU. Pero...

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Hindi po totally. Marami pong financial permutations na puwedeng mangyari on an actuarial basis. So importante din po talaga itong pag-aralan on an actuarial and sustainable basis.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: Pero ang basic po doon: sa ngayon, kayo, dapat may contribution?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: It depends po on when and how. Sa ngayon po, nakatutok po at punong-puno ngayon yung ating sundalo dahil halos 90% na yung fill-up. Hindi po ako, in conscience, puwedeng humingi sa kanila ng contribution sa ngayon. And we are requiring them to do more, insofar as I'm concerned.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: So kayo, sa ngayon, tingin ninyo hindi dapat hingan ng contribution?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Hindi po dapat. Tingnan po natin kung may sustainable na programa na kakayanin naman po nila at patas po sa kanila; we will consider it. We will be open to it. All proposals for easing the fiscal burden are open, but there are no definitives until we see the plan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: Hindi po bago yung mga proposals for pension reform. I mean, sa totoo lang, nung una akong pumasok sa Kongreso, pinag-uusapan na po ito. I would imagine, nung nasa Kongreso pa kayo, issue na rin ito. At isa sa mga proposal doon po doon na yung mga bagong papasok, sa kanila ipapatupad yung contribution system. Ibig sabihin, yung mga nasa servisyo na, pwedeng hindi na. Sabi nyo nga, parang may kontrata yan, nung pumasok sila, kailangang i-fulfill yun. Pero sa mga bago, hindi ba pwedeng ganon?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Actually po, that would make sense because then you have time for the pension plan to mature. So that, may drawdown. Pag unang drawdown po doon sa pension system na iyon, yung mga nag-contribute na magbe-benefit. So i-carry na lang yung mga [unclear]. Siyempre, maaari din po iyon. Iyon nga lang, pag-aralan lang po natin yung optional at mandatory retirements kasi baka naman po maubos yung optional at makaapekto din yung pension sa kung magkano ang sahod. Depende na po sa actuarial. Lalo-lalo na po kung may legislated benefits. Iyon po ang problema. Iyon po ang kakain sa buhay ng pondo. But, you know, sa bagong entry po na mag-contribution, and then if you can design a pension system that will benefit them to allow the system to mature, why not? We can consider it all.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: Okay. May baka tanong pa, pero let me move on to another issue. Recently, the Secretary made statements regarding Chinese language teaching and cultural exchange sa mga Filipino-Chinese schools dito sa Pilipinas. Could you elaborate on your concern regarding this?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: It was a matter of concern, Your Honor, because it was reported that the training was done by Jinan University. And Jinan University was the source of the supposed study that Batanes was part of China. And we all know, Your Honor, that this is a state university, and depending on how you look at things, I think if it's state-sponsored, then you mean party-sponsored. And so, it is a matter of concern that even as a normal parent, that Chinese language teachers who may even be teaching minors are coming from the same institution that published these kinds of supposed academic studies. It's a matter of concern, but our agency has alerted other agencies, and we're not actively pursuing anything on it.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: Mayroon po kayong statement sa isang Kapihan sa Manila Bay Forum. Sabi ninyo rito na malaking ebidensya na itong mga eskwelahan ay ginagamit sa malign influence. Ang tinutukoy ninyo po ay yung mga local Filipino-Chinese schools. Hindi naman lahat, pero mayroon diyang malign influence. Kaya dapat maging masusi tayo, hindi lamang sa university kundi sa mga mababang paaralan kung saan may cultural and language and other exchanges. Sabi ninyo po may ebidensya, malaking ebidensya na may mga eskwelahan.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: It's res ipsa loquitur on their part. If they publish something, I was referring to the university, Jinan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: So ang tinutukoy ninyo po rito ay yung university, hindi yung mga school. I-clarify po natin kasi very sensitive po ito.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Yes, I beg to clarify. Thank the gentleman for asking the clarification. It's [unclear] University because...

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: So hindi ninyo po tinutukoy yung mga local Chinese schools?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: We have no evidence.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: You have no evidence?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Yes, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: Okay, thank you for that clarification. Kasi nga po, parang ang... We don't want to cause panic.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Yes, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: Yes, especially among the Filipino-Chinese community.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: Okay. Now, of course, sangayon tayo na talagang kabalbalan yung claim nung Jinan University na ang Batanes ay bahagi ng Pilipinas. Pero itong... Let me wind up, Madam Chair. Itong issue na to ay nagmula sa isang report ng SeaLight. Ayan po, that is the report. The university that said batanes is China is also training Manila's Chinese teachers. Okay. This is an article published by Juan Ray Powell, the director of SeaLight. Ngayon, itong SeaLight po, are you aware of the funding and the origins of SeaLight?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: I'm not aware of the funding, Your Honor, but I know the individual.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: Si Ray Powell?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Yes, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: Of course. Si Ray Powell, of course, is actually laman ng balita yan, lumalabas sa media often, and he talks about these issues. Now, next slide po. Actually, yung kanyang SeaLight, you are... I don't know, maybe... Ito ang lumalabas po, na yung kanyang SeaLight is a project of the Gordian Knot Center for... The Gordian Knot Center for Strategic Innovation. Tama po. Is that correct?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: I'm not in a position to confirm or deny, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: Next slide po. Yung Gordian Knot Center for... Sorry, it's called Stanford University's Gordian Knot Center for National Security Innovation. Okay. According to this article published on the navy.mil website, meaning to say U.S. Navy, website, this was established by the Office of Naval Research, which is a part of the U.S. Navy. So, next slide. And so, the director, ayan na po, the Office of Naval Research, which is part of the U.S. Navy. And, next slide. Yung kanyang Sea... This is the social media Twitter account of Ray Powell, and his handle is Gordian Knot Ray. Yun yung koneksyon. So, in other words, itong si Ray Powell, na aktibong-aktibo sa media ng Pilipinas, and in fact, sets the media agenda, dahil siya yung unang naglabas nung report regarding the Chinese University, apparently, ay, you know, nakaugnay pala sa U.S. Navy. Yung kanyang center ay tinatag ng U.S. Navy. So, hindi po ba maituturing din ito? In the same way na yung ginagawa ng China ay tinatawag na foreign information manipulation and interference, ay, di ba, pwede rin, dapat din ituring na foreign information manipulation, and interference, ang SeaLight at itong si Ray Powell. In other words, kailangan may disclosure din, at may transparency at disclosure sa pinanggagalingan ditong Ray Powell, at madalas na sina-cite ng DND, ng Coast Guard, si Admiral Tarriela, at iba pa.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: I think that that's up to him to address, Your Honor. For the Gordian Knot Center to address. For us, we have our own independent sources. Now, what's important here is what the information is. Is it accurate or not? When we compare a Batanes narrative with activities in the West Philippine Sea, the proof of the pudding is in the eating. And what we are after in foreign malign influence is misinformation. So, and, and, not information per se, it's misinformation. So, at the end of the day, the credibility will lie on who has the more accurate information. But in terms of his connections, that is for him to disclose.

segments.speaker: Rep. Antonio L. Tinio
segments.text: Of course. Okay. So, agad ko na lang po yung tanong ko, pero meron pa akong mga tanong. So, next round na lang po. Thank you, Madam Chair.

segments.speaker: Rep. Bella Vanessa B. Suansing
segments.text: Yes. Thank you. Thank you, Congressman Tinio. Next to interpolate from the majority, Representative Johanne Bautista.

segments.speaker: Rep. Johanne Monich G. Bautista
segments.text: Thank you, Madam Chair. And good morning po to the members of the committee, my fellow colleagues, and of course, Secretary Teodoro and the DND family. Magandang umaga po sa inyong lahat. I will be asking questions po pertaining to our uniform personnel. I'm not sure if it's classified information. To ask, more or less, ilan po ba ang ating uniform personnel? And if that is classified information, may I ask, Madam Chair, magkano po ba sa pondo ng department ang allocated for the uniforms and fabrics of our uniform personnel, more or less, Madam Chair?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: For the uniform personnel, Your Honor, we have 162,000. As for the clothing, I'm not too sure. Your Honor, because we have to aggregate, the clothing is per service. We don't have the aggregated amount at this time. But we can provide you with the information.

segments.speaker: Rep. Johanne Monich G. Bautista
segments.text: All right, Madam Chair. We can await that figures. The reason I'm asking this, Madam Chair, is that pertaining to RA 9242 or the Philippine Tropical Fabrics, this was passed in 2004, and this requires the use of Philippine Tropical Fabrics for government uniforms and to support locally manufactured products, local resources, and promote employment, no? This is for our local industries. Particularly po, yung IRR po niya, strengthened implementation by requiring local sourcing and the DOST PTRI testing and certification, and there are also allowed exemptions. In other words, it is not enough that our uniforms are made in the country, it is required that we use a certain amount of Philippine fabrics. So, may we ask kung wala man pong ano for the department, Madam Chair, to submit if they have projected figures on what would the budget to be spent on RA 9242 compliant Philippine-made fabrics. Madam Chair.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: I don't have the figure right now, Your Honor, because the fabric must not only be Philippine-made, but must conform to minimum standards of safety and fireproofing that we have. We know that an indigenous fabric industry is hard to get, because we don't have indigenous cotton and other fabrics which actually cannot be substituted based on the safety considerations. Nonetheless, Your Honor, we will provide you with the information, and it's not a question of the manufacturer, really. It's the sourcing of the fabric, and we have to resource fabric, actually, to more trusted sources, meaning to say countries which, if at all, are not involved in disputes with us.

segments.speaker: Rep. Johanne Monich G. Bautista
segments.text: Thank you for that, Madam Chair and Mr. Secretary. Now, going to the issue of local sourcing, Madam Chair, if the Philippine manufacturers cannot yet supply all of the, or at least some of, the uniform requirements or meet certain military specifications, meron po bang ginagawa ang department together with the DOST, PTRI, and the local industry to at least address that gap and eventually comply with this law?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Thank you for the question, Your Honor. Honestly, I have not had the chance to devote time with the DOST and with the local fabric industry, because I'm really concerned now on our supply chains more than anything. So, it's something I'll schedule to look into it on a department-wide basis. But then, it will depend also on the production of, and the agricultural production that we have for cotton. And I know that for silk, for example, for parachutes, there were some who tried to venture into silk, but there was no market unless silk was branded with a country. So, the experiments failed.

segments.speaker: Rep. Johanne Monich G. Bautista
segments.text: Thank you, Madam Chair. Actually, I think the IRR of the law that I'm mentioning, only requires 5% to use Philippine fabrics. And I believe that the Army, under former General Navarrete, I read somewhere that they actually started meeting with the DOST on the matter. Now, I think as regards the issue of local sourcing, it's just a suggestion and maybe the department can also help by providing maybe projected needs. In order for us to help develop our local industry for the fabrics. And at the same time, comply po with the requirement of using at least 5% of Philippine fabric for our uniforms, Madam Chair.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: I was informed to the Honorable Representative and Madam Chair that the issue there is our battle dress uniforms, which have safety standards. But for the general office attire, I think there is some component of Philippine fabrics and of course the office barongs.

segments.speaker: Rep. Johanne Monich G. Bautista
segments.text: Yes, Madam Chair. Just to me, if we are able to communicate the needed requirements, standards, then hopefully maybe we can help develop or grow that industry and locally source our own products for the making of our uniforms, Madam Chair.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: I think, Your Honor, I will welcome the idea because locally made should not necessarily be locally grown, just as long as the growing is on a Philippine [unclear] country basis, like the experiment made with the beef industry before, where we had no grazing land and the original plan was to have a beef or cattle industry somewhere else where land was cheap and just imported for the Philippines. So we really have to be creative about these arrangements that we make, particularly if all our arable land is for food production rather than non-food items.

segments.speaker: Rep. Johanne Monich G. Bautista
segments.text: Thank you, Madam Chair. I think that's a very valuable suggestion. We welcome it. Yes, Madam Chair and Mr. Secretary. And anyway, the requirement so far of the law is only 5% of the entire uniform, I think. Now, moving on, Madam Chair, under RA 12024 or the Self-Reliant Defense Posture Law, it directs the government to strengthen the local defense industry, support in-country enterprises, promote technology transfer, develop resilient supply chains, and prioritize local employment. For the 2027 budget, Madam Chair, can the Department provide us on how much procurement or program spending is expected to support local production, local maintenance, Filipino suppliers, more or less, Madam Chair?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: There will be, honestly speaking, none, Your Honor. Why? The law is fatally flawed. It does not provide for co-equity and co-investment, and it does not provide for research and development. So it will not meet the needs of a future armed force. So unless you put in the law provision for equity or research and development, there will be no right-thinking producer of technology that will allow you to benefit on the upside when you do not share the risk of the downside. That is a simple value proposition, Your Honor. Because the most important thing is not the production, even though 100% production is done outside. It's the intellectual property rights that are important, that you have equal rights to the IPR. That is the key and the cornerstone. If you cannot acquire the intellectual property rights, then you have no rights at all, even though you are co-producing. There will be no technology transfer. That's a value proposition that those who have been in the private sector know and know fully well.

segments.speaker: Rep. Johanne Monich G. Bautista
segments.text: Thank you, Madam Chair and Mr. Secretary, for that very straightforward answer. And I think it is the position of the Secretary that there is a need to amend this law?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Definitely, Your Honor. And you can download the R&D for it to the DOST. If you don't have a budget for risk capital, then you cannot derive any benefits whatsoever. It's just like people in the mining industry. If you don't spend for the exploration, which is risky, I mean, how can you value something properly?

segments.speaker: Rep. Johanne Monich G. Bautista
segments.text: Thank you, Madam Chair and Mr. Secretary. Just wanted to thank the Secretary and commit to look into the proposed suggestions of Mr. Secretary to amend the law and ensure its implementation. Thank you, Madam Chair.

segments.speaker: Rep. Bella Vanessa B. Suansing
segments.text: Thank you, Congressman Johanne Bautista. Uh, at this point, I would like to acknowledge the additional, uh, House members, um, who are present today. Uh, Congressman Junard "Ahong" Chan, uh, Vice Chair Joboy Aquino, uh, Representative J.J. Romualdo, Representative Ferdinand Beltran, Representative Elijah San Fernando, Assistant Majority Leader De Carlo "Oyo" Uy, and Representative Samier Tan. Next to interpolate, from the minority, Congressman Egay Erice.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: Good morning, Secretary Teodoro and the rest of the DND family. My father was my late father was a former member of the Philippine Air Force. A non-commissioned officer before he worked with Air America in Vietnam. So we have a long relations with the U.S. At the same time, we have also a very long relations with China. With the U.S. militarily, with China, economically. So foreign policy really is as I see it now, it's really, you know, I think there's a divergence between the statements of President Marcos and Secretary Teodoro. Well, it might be a strategic way of doing things, but there's also dangers. So let me just let me just for example, President Marcos says that we need a reset in terms of relations with China. Secretary Teodoro says broader defense engagement with China is impossible because China lacks good faith. Marcos says China remains an important investment and economic partner. Secretary Teodoro says China uses coercion, blackmail, and foreign influence. President Marcos discusses joint oil exploration. Meanwhile, the Philippine defense system becomes increasingly interoperable with the United States, especially with the EDCA sites. So, there might be a decline on the trust on both countries, the U.S. and China. Ayoko na pong ayoko pong pangunahan yung strategy as a strategy. As I very well know that the President is the chief architect of foreign policy. However, there are public concerns. At ito po yung gusto ko sana itanong. First question, po, Secretary. What exactly triggers the Mutual Defense Treaty?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: The triggering of Article 5 of the Mutual Defense Treaty, is a call of the Philippine government or the U.S. government if an attack is made on either country, public vessel, and the like. So, the trigger really is a call of an executive or the triggering party. Here, it will be the President of the Philippines based on an attack, or any public vessel, if he feels that Article 5, which is the active portion of the Mutual Defense Treaty, comes into play.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: What happens if China and the U.S. engage in the Taiwan War? What are the possibilities of the Philippines participating in this?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: The President has made clear, Your Honor, that the Philippines is constitutionally prohibited from engaging in foreign—

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: Pardon?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: The President has made clear that the Philippines is prohibited from engaging in any offensive activity, so it's purely defensive.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: But the U.S. might use the EDCA sites, several EDCA sites in the Philippines to launch their attacks.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: That's a speculative thing, might, but it has not.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: It's a reality.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Under the President's guidance, it cannot.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: So it remains to be speculative as far as you are concerned?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Oh, sure, Your Honor. It's speculative, but insofar as the President's guidance is concerned, it cannot be used for any external factor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: Can they use the Philippine territory during the Taiwan conflict?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: The EDCA sites? It can only be used if, Your Honor, the Philippines is under attack or threat.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: So this is very clear in the...

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Oh, yes, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: ...in the treaty.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: It is clear. And under the agreement on enhanced defense cooperation, it cannot violate any Philippine law or the Constitution.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: Could U.S. offensive missiles be permanently positioned here?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: If they're with the Philippines, Your Honor, then we will welcome them if they're under the Philippine armed forces.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: Pardon, Mr. Secretary, I can barely hear you.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: The Philippine arsenal, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: so they can launch a missile attack to China?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: The Philippines will launch, Your Honor, if ever. If they become part of the armed forces of the Philippines, we will welcome them.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: So your answer is they cannot use offensive missiles from Philippine territory? From Philippine territory.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: No, Your Honor, for offensive purposes, unless Article 5 is activated. It's to defend the Philippines.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: And what is our long-term West Philippine Sea Objective?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: The long-term West Philippine Sea Objective, Your Honor, it remains the same under the Constitution. It's to explore and exploit for the Filipinos each and every item in there that we can.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: So, how would you relate this to the pronouncement of the President that we can have joint oil exploration to China?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Well, that's subject to Philippine law, Your Honor, and the Constitution.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: And it, when it comes to, because, you know, there are millions of Filipino-Chinese here in the Philippines. In fact, Secretary Teodoro, you are a Cojuangco with Chinese roots. Am I right?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Oh, yeah. Seven generations ago.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: Yes, yes. And I talked to the Filipino Chinese Chamber of Commerce here. There are about 200,000 or more Chinese who illegally enter the Philippines with fake documents provided by agencies of our government. And they are not now so worried with what's happening even when, for example, when you conducted a raid involving [unclear]—

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Oh, yes, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: —in Cagayan de Oro.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: And where is it located, Your Honor?

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: The Philippine Veterans Industrial Estate.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Yes. That is a supervised agency under DND.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: So, there is no business for anyone doing illegal activities in there. Doing what?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Illegal activities, Your Honor. Which is why there is a closure order by DENR and a revocation of its ECC.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: And can the civilian agencies do that—

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: or—

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Of course, Your Honor. Yes.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: And why would the DND be involved?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Because PHIVIDEC, Your Honor, is a supervised agency under DND.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: A supervised agency?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: It is a GOCC supervised by DND.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: So the GOCC is under DND?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: It is attached to DND.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: Attached to DND.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Yes, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: And the DND under 6975 still has a mandate for internal and national security. Okay. Can you specifically state what's the illegal activity?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: Producing substandard steel, Your Honor, which did not pass regulations. Environmental damage, Your Honor. Having radioactively tainted scrap metals in there. And danger to the workers.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: But no espionage or military issues?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: The military issue there, Your Honor, was it was in PHIVIDEC. Jurisdictionally.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: Oh, okay. Under the DND. There's no allegation that's being used by the Chinese government for any espionage activity or something?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: There is no evidence, Your Honor, but I will leave that to the law enforcement authorities, the NBI, who actually got a warrant, search warrant from a court before entering into the area. Yes. And these are law enforcement operations. Before doing so, a search warrant valid was taken, Your Honor. It was not a unilateral entry without judicial authority.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: And there's also the case of Joseph Sy, a mining owner here in the Philippines who has fake documents and he was being incarcerated for at least for almost a year. And there's also an allegation that he's a Chinese government spy. Do you have any information on that?

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: The allegation I know of Joseph Sy, Your Honor, is fake citizenship. No espionage issue. As far as I know, there was none. It's a BI issue, Your Honor.

segments.speaker: Rep. Edgar R. Erice
segments.text: It's a BI issue. Yeah. Thank you, Secretary. Thank you.

segments.speaker: DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.
segments.text: You're most welcome.
